problems.title: A square root bounded below by a negative number
problems.question: Solve √(x+5)≥−5.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity, then check domains, signs and counting assumptions.
formulas: A real square root is nonnegative.
steps: The inequality is automatic wherever the radical exists. Its domain is x+5≥0.

problems.title: Count four-digit multiples of five
problems.question: How many four-digit positive integers are divisible by 5?
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity, then check domains, signs and counting assumptions.
formulas: A multiple of 5 ends in 0 or 5.
steps: The thousands digit has 9 choices, the middle digits 10 each, and last digit 2. Total=9×10×10×2=1800.

problems.title: Equal square roots with an invalid algebraic root
problems.question: Find the sum of solutions of √(x²−2x−2)=√(2x²−7x+4).
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity, then check domains, signs and counting assumptions.
formulas: Equal nonnegative square roots require equal, nonnegative radicands.
steps: Equating radicands gives x²−5x+6=(x−2)(x−3)=0.
At x=2 both radicands are −2, invalid. At x=3 both are 1, valid. The root sum is 3.

problems.title: A vector-sum length from a difference length
problems.question: |a|=7,|b|=11,|a−b|=14. Find |a+b|.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity, then check domains, signs and counting assumptions.
steps: |a+b|²=2(49+121)−196=144. Take the nonnegative square root.

problems.title: A homothety about an off-origin centre
problems.question: Centre O=(2,7),scale k=3. Find the image of B=(1,3).
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity, then check domains, signs and counting assumptions.

problems.title: Pascal’s identity in a quotient
problems.question: Evaluate $\binom{16}6/[\binom{14}5+\binom{14}6+\binom{15}5]$.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity, then check domains, signs and counting assumptions.
steps: The first two denominator terms sum to C(15,6). Adding C(15,5) gives C(16,6), exactly the numerator.

problems.title: A point three eighths along a spatial segment
problems.question: M=(1,2,3),N=(3,4,7). K divides MK:KN=3:5. Find K.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity, then check domains, signs and counting assumptions.

problems.title: A strict radical inequality
problems.question: Solve √(2x+5)<x+1.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity, then check domains, signs and counting assumptions.
formulas: Domain x≥−5/2 and strict positivity of the right side require x>−1.
steps: After squaring, 2x+5<(x+1)² gives x²>4. Intersect x<−2 or x>2 with x>−1.
The solution is x>2.

problems.title: A collinear vector with a prescribed dot product
problems.question: a=(1,2,−3). Find x parallel to a with x·a=28.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity, then check domains, signs and counting assumptions.

problems.title: Volume of a regular hexagonal prism
problems.question: Base side is 2 and height √3. Find the volume.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity, then check domains, signs and counting assumptions.
steps: The base area is 6√3. Multiplying by height √3 gives 18.

problems.title: Third term of a binomial expansion
problems.question: Find the third term of (x+3)⁷.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity, then check domains, signs and counting assumptions.
formulas: The third term uses exponent index 2: C(7,2)x⁵3².
steps: C(7,2)=21 and 3²=9, giving 189x⁵.

problems.title: Cancel factorials with admissible indices
problems.question: Solve $A_x^4 P_{x-4}/P_{x-2}=42$, where Pₙ=n!.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity, then check domains, signs and counting assumptions.
steps: The left side simplifies to x!/(x−2)!=x(x−1). Thus x²−x−42=(x−7)(x+6)=0.
Only x=7 is an admissible integer index.

problems.title: Equivalent empty solution sets
problems.question: For which a are √(x−3)=a and √(x−7)<−x²+2x−3 equivalent?
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity, then check domains, signs and counting assumptions.
formulas: The second right side is −(x−1)²−2<0, while its left side is nonnegative.
steps: The inequality has no real solutions. The equation must therefore also have no solutions, which occurs exactly for a<0.
For a≥0 the equation has the valid root x=a²+3.

problems.title: A three-dimensional cross product
problems.question: Find (2,−3,5)×(4,2,−6).
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity, then check domains, signs and counting assumptions.

problems.title: Possible lengths of a collinear sum
problems.question: Collinear vectors have lengths 199,19,9. Which listed length can |a+2b+3c| have?
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity, then check domains, signs and counting assumptions.
formulas: Relative directions give the absolute values of ±199±38±27.
steps: Up to reversing every sign, the possible lengths are 264,210,188,134.
Only 188 is listed; it is attained by 199−38+27.

problems.title: Choose a root uniformly from a finite set
problems.question: Choose uniformly from {2,4,7,1,3,8,−2,−6}. Find the chance it solves (x−3)√(x²−5x+4)=0.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity, then check domains, signs and counting assumptions.
formulas: Radicand=(x−1)(x−4); a product can vanish at a valid zero of either factor.
steps: The radical zeros x=1,4 are valid. x=3 makes the radicand negative, so is not a solution.
Two of the eight choices work, giving 1/4.

problems.title: A cubic radical equation and its sign restriction
problems.question: Solve √(3x³−13x²+4x+4)=x−2.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity, then check domains, signs and counting assumptions.
steps: Squaring and subtracting gives 3x³−14x²+8x=x(3x−2)(x−4)=0.
The candidates are 0,2/3,4. Only 4 satisfies x≥2 and the original equation.

problems.title: Integer terms of a radical binomial expansion
problems.question: How many of the 51 terms in (∛4+⁵√3)⁵⁰ are positive integers?
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity, then check domains, signs and counting assumptions.
steps: Prime exponents must be integers: 3 divides 50−k and 5 divides k. Hence k≡2 mod3 and k≡0 mod5.
The allowed indices are 5,20,35,50. Their coefficients and prime powers are integers.

problems.title: Direction cosines to three coordinate axes
problems.question: A nonzero vector makes 60° with the positive y and z directions. Find its cosine to the positive x direction.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity, then check domains, signs and counting assumptions.
steps: The last two squared cosines are 1/4 each. Thus cos²alpha=1/2, giving cos alpha=±√2/2.

problems.title: Volume using a normal prism section
problems.question: An oblique triangular prism has lateral edge 8 and perpendicular cross-section area 5. Find volume.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity, then check domains, signs and counting assumptions.
steps: V=5×8=40. This is the same base-times-perpendicular-height volume expressed in a different direction.

problems.title: Conjugates with odd and even exponents
problems.question: Which are irrational: A=(√5−2)²⁰²²+(√5+2)²⁰²²; B=(√6−3)²⁰²¹+(√6+3)²⁰²¹; C=(√5−2)²⁰²²(√5+2)²⁰²¹?
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity, then check domains, signs and counting assumptions.
formulas: Binomial terms with odd powers of the rational summand cancel when adding conjugate-sign expressions.
steps: A retains only even powers of √5 and is an integer. B retains only odd powers of √6, so it is a nonzero integer multiple of √6 and is irrational.
The factors √5−2 and √5+2 multiply to 1, so C=√5−2, also irrational.

problems.title: Nonempty subsets of six quiz topics
problems.question: A ticket contains one or more of six distinct topics; order does not matter. How many tickets?
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity, then check domains, signs and counting assumptions.
formulas: A set of n elements has 2ⁿ subsets.
steps: There are 2⁶=64 subsets, including the empty one. Excluding it leaves 63.

problems.title: A sedan’s factory of origin
problems.question: Factory1 makes 30% sedans,Factory2 60%. In the combined showroom 40% are sedans. Find probability a chosen sedan is from Factory1.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity, then check domains, signs and counting assumptions.
formulas: Use the mixture equation, then conditional probability.
steps: If p is Factory1’s stock share, 0.3p+0.6(1−p)=0.4 gives p=2/3.
Factory1 sedans are 0.3×2/3=0.2 of all cars. Divide by sedan fraction 0.4: probability=1/2.

problems.title: Reflect a line in the diagonal axis
problems.question: Reflect y=2x in y=x.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity, then check domains, signs and counting assumptions.
steps: Swapping gives x=2y, hence y=x/2.

problems.title: Sum vectors from a point to four parallelogram vertices
problems.question: O is the diagonal intersection of parallelogram ABCD and M≠O. Find k for MA+MB+MC+MD=kMO.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity, then check domains, signs and counting assumptions.
formulas: O is the midpoint of AC and BD.
steps: MA+MC=2MO and MB+MD=2MO. Adding gives 4MO. Since MO≠0, k=4.
